chapter: Willy Lewis band in Paris and Egypt
title: Alexandria: the Greek owner Pastudes, hotel pounds and Stardust
summary: In Alexandria the owner Pastudes treated the band lavishly; Butler took a cheaper room and won over a cold audience with a Stardust solo.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Now, what was working in Egypt like?

Beautiful. They had a man, his name was Pastudes (PHONETIC). This man was the feigningest man I'd ever seen, but this man was a handsome man, a Greek, Pastudes. Pastudes could smile and look like an angel, and he was a dark-complected man. And get mad and look like a devil looking at you, really.

And pastudez, we went down there to work and Pastudes -- each man had his bottle of champagne when he wanted it. And anything else that he needs. So guys was going down there. At the time the hotel was $30.00 a day. But he had -- the hotel, it had everything. Service and everything.
Now, where were you playing, in Cairo?

No, Alexandria. I always watched that. I said, well, look, you know, what are we paying $30.00 for everyday? And I said, I can't pay that, get me one of those rooms way upstairs. He said, 'Good boy. You got this room for $8.' That was pounds, and we got paid off in pounds. So at that time that was about, pound ble was $15.00.
So I said, well, I don't go anywhere until I save something. So all right, we were friends. So the first night we started playing, we played but they didn't respond.

Yes. Alexandria. And this band had all its friends, and everything. So I said, give me "Stardust". I jumped out there and I did a little Armstrong, got up there and did "Stardust" and hit the notes on the end (inaudible) and that broke the house open. It broke it open and then it was beautiful. Oh, it was beautiful. And I couldn't understand why Willy and them was living in the hotel paying $35.00 a day. But the man was so proud he says, "I own all the bread, I own all the ice cream. I own all the dope." So I didn't bother with that. Some of them cats in the band was going crazy ---happy.
So it seems like the man told us, I pay my musicians 50 pounds a day. So after that (inaudible). And that man was laying something on me like 10 pounds a day.
